title: The Conversation as a Test: Golden Transcripts of a Device Session, and Ignoring Exactly What Should Differ

questions.question: Why record a whole session as a test instead of writing the expected value for each reply?
options: It catches what a reply-at-a-time test misses: a firmware change that adds a byte to every reply, or a reordering, and it is recorded and not composed
questions.explanation: The conversation as a whole is what breaks.

questions.question: A transcript file has a line `> 0102`. What should the reader do?
options: Refuse it: line 1, bytes are two hexadecimal digits each, since two bytes with no space look like one number
questions.explanation: A half read golden file must never be used.

questions.question: Why does compare report only the first difference?
options: After the first one everything that follows is out of step, and a second report is noise
questions.explanation: It names where: message and byte.

questions.question: Replies carry a time of day at bytes 2 to 5 and it differs every run. What is the remedy?
options: A mask over exactly those bytes of replies: without it the first difference was message 1 byte 2, with it none
questions.explanation: The test would otherwise fail every day.

questions.question: A mask covers bytes 2 to 5 of replies. A request's byte 1 and a reply's byte 6 are changed. What happens?
options: Both are caught: the mask covers only the direction and the bytes it was given for
questions.explanation: A reading one byte past the masked time was caught at message 1, byte 6.

questions.question: New firmware adds a byte to every reply. What does the golden transcript say?
options: Length, at message 1 and offset 8: the first reply is longer and the shorter one ended at 8
questions.explanation: A protocol change no one announced.
